title: Fund the Defence Investment Plan's remaining £4.7bn
headline: The plan's own explainer says £4.7bn is still to be found at this Budget.
description: The Defence Investment Plan is funded mainly by reallocating budgets across government, with £10.3bn identified when it was published. Its funding explainer says a further £4.7bn over four years will be confirmed at Budget 2026. This lever confirms it: £4.7bn spread evenly over the plan's four years, as new day-to-day and capital spending on defence rather than money taken from other departments. The department's own document is the source of the total; the even spread is our assumption.

baselinePolicy.text: The March forecast includes the Spending Review 2025 defence settlement and the OBR's path towards 3% of GDP by 2030-31. It does not include the £4.7bn the Defence Investment Plan's explainer says is still to be confirmed.

source.quote: A further £4.7 billion over four years will be confirmed at Budget 2026, in a fair and balanced way.

It is funded primarily by reallocating budget from across government departments, with £10.3 billion identified now. A further £4.7 billion over four years will be confirmed at Budget 2026, in a fair and balanced way.

terms.label: Funding still to be confirmed over the plan's four years

source.quote: A further £4.7 billion over four years will be confirmed at Budget 2026

terms.label: Share of the total in each year, spread evenly

source.note: The explainer gives a four-year total and no profile. An even spread is our assumption.

rawSource.note: The total is the department's own; the even profile is ours. Nothing is committed beyond the plan's four years, so 2030-31 is nought.

caveats: The explainer says the money will be found 'in a fair and balanced way', which in the plan means reallocation from other departments. This lever instead funds it as new spending, which is the choice a Chancellor makes when no other department will give it up.
An even spread over four years is our assumption. The plan publishes a total, not a profile.
The 43% capital share is the Spending Review's own split of the defence settlement, applied here because the plan is mostly equipment.

considerations.text: The government has published the plan and told Parliament how much of it is funded. Refusing the remaining £4.7bn at this Budget does not cancel the commitments the plan makes; it leaves them to be found from other budgets.
The same explainer restates the NATO commitment to 3.5% of GDP by 2035 and the aim of 3% in the next Parliament. Filling this gap is a step on that path, not the path itself.

sources.quote: the UK has committed to reach 3.5% of GDP on defence spending by 2035

considerations.text: No Barnett consequentials: defence is a reserved matter and the Statement of Funding Policy gives the Ministry of Defence no comparability factor.
